subject: API Design

findings.subject: API Design
findings.title: OpenAPI spec's /testing/reset path omits the version segment the controller actually requires
findings.recommendation: Regenerate docs/PilotUtilityApi_v1.json from the running app (or add it to CI) so the documented path includes the required `v{version}` segment, e.g. `/v1/testing/reset`.

findings.subject: API Design
findings.title: Spec documents a ProblemDetails body for the 400 response, but the controller returns an empty BadRequest with only a custom header

evidence.excerpt:
Response.Headers.Append("Warning", response.ErrorMessage ?? "An error occurred");
return BadRequest();

findings.recommendation: Return `BadRequest(new ProblemDetails { Detail = response.ErrorMessage })` so the actual response body matches the documented `ProblemDetails` schema, or update the spec to match the header-only contract.

strengths.subject: API Design
strengths.title: An OpenAPI 3.1 spec is generated and checked in, backed by Scalar/Swashbuckle UI wiring in code

strengths.subject: API Design
strengths.title: The API is explicitly versioned via Asp.Versioning, with version-neutral system endpoints kept separate

checkResults.subject: API Design
checkResults.reason: Visual inspection shows well-formed OpenAPI 3.1 JSON; not run through a formal validator.

checkResults.subject: API Design
checkResults.reason: The documented /testing/reset path and 400 response body diverge from the actual versioned route and response.

checkResults.subject: API Design
checkResults.reason: Endpoints are small in number; the one action-style endpoint (testing/reset) is a reasonable exception for a utility/admin operation, not a resource collection.

notes: API Design is applicable: an OpenAPI spec exists and two controllers implement it. The spec is a stale/manually-exported snapshot that has drifted from the actual versioned routes and error contract.
